bib.title: Chapter 7: Working with Text Data (Introduction to Machine Learning with Python)
bib.venue: O'Reilly book chapter (authors, year and book title are not printed in the chapter text)

question: How should text strings be turned into numeric features (bag-of-words, tf-idf, n-grams, normalization, topic models) for scikit-learn models, shown on IMDb sentiment classification?
contributions: Walks through CountVectorizer, min_df, stopwords, TfidfVectorizer, n-grams, lemmatization vs stemming and LDA on the IMDb reviews, with CV scores.

results.claim: Bag-of-words on IMDb train reviews yields a 74,849-word vocabulary.
results.setup: IMDb Maas dataset, 25,000 train / 25,000 test reviews, balanced; LogisticRegression, GridSearchCV C in [0.001..10], cv=5; default CountVectorizer
results.quote: The shape of X_train, the bag-of-words representation of the training data, is 25,000×74,849

results.claim: Logistic regression on raw counts gets 88% mean 5-fold CV accuracy with default C.
results.setup: IMDb Maas dataset, 25,000 train / 25,000 test reviews, balanced; LogisticRegression, GridSearchCV C in [0.001..10], cv=5; CountVectorizer defaults

results.claim: Tuning C (best C=0.1) lifts CV accuracy to 89%; test accuracy is 88%.
results.setup: IMDb Maas dataset, 25,000 train / 25,000 test reviews, balanced; LogisticRegression, GridSearchCV C in [0.001..10], cv=5; CountVectorizer defaults; test accuracy 0.88

results.claim: min_df=5 cuts the vocabulary from 74,849 to 27,271 features with no change in CV accuracy (0.89).
results.setup: IMDb Maas dataset, 25,000 train / 25,000 test reviews, balanced; LogisticRegression, GridSearchCV C in [0.001..10], cv=5; CountVectorizer(min_df=5)
results.quote: bring down the number of features to 27,271

results.claim: Built-in English stopword list has 318 words.
Stopwords removal drops only 305 features (27,271 to 26,966) and CV accuracy falls from 0.89 to 0.88, so not worth it here.
results.setup: IMDb Maas dataset, 25,000 train / 25,000 test reviews, balanced; LogisticRegression, GridSearchCV C in [0.001..10], cv=5; CountVectorizer(min_df=5, stop_words='english')

results.claim: tf-idf (min_df=5, norm=None) pipeline with logistic regression gives CV accuracy 0.89, a slight gain over counts.
results.setup: IMDb Maas dataset, 25,000 train / 25,000 test reviews, balanced; LogisticRegression, GridSearchCV C in [0.001..10], cv=5; make_pipeline(TfidfVectorizer(min_df=5, norm=None), LogisticRegression())
results.quote: As you can see, there is some improvement when using tf–idf instead of just word counts.
results.note: Printed score equals the 0.89 for counts at two-decimal precision; the improvement is asserted in text, not visible in the printed numbers.

results.claim: Adding bigrams and trigrams with tf-idf raises CV accuracy to 0.91 (best ngram_range (1,3), C=100).
results.setup: IMDb Maas dataset, 25,000 train / 25,000 test reviews, balanced; LogisticRegression, GridSearchCV C in [0.001..10], cv=5 with C grid extended to 100; TfidfVectorizer(min_df=5), ngram_range in (1,1),(1,2),(1,3)

limits: Single dataset (IMDb) and single classifier (logistic regression); CV scores printed to 2 decimals, no variance.
CV scores at 0.88/0.89 cannot distinguish min_df, stopwords or tf-idf effects.
Author notes cross-validation with CountVectorizer is valid only because default settings collect no statistics; Pipeline preferred (fn 6).
LDA is randomized: changing random_state can give quite different topics; interpretations should be verified against documents.
Dated: scikit-learn API (get_feature_names, n_topics, n_iter), spaCy 1.x 'en' model and tokens_from_list; word2vec and RNNs are outside the scope, no transformers.
practices: Check whether a string feature is categorical, a free string mappable to categories, structured, or real text before choosing treatment (p.324).
Avoid manually entered values for concepts better captured as categorical variables (p.324).

Strip HTML such as
before vectorizing (p.327).
For high-dimensional sparse data like BoW, linear models such as LogisticRegression often work best (p.332).
Use min_df to drop rare tokens: fewer features, faster, more interpretable, same accuracy (p.333-334).
Fixed stopword lists are mostly helpful for small datasets; alternative is max_df (p.335).
Use a Pipeline with TfidfVectorizer so idf statistics are fit inside CV folds only (p.336).
Include unigrams, adding bigrams helps in most cases; longer n-grams up to 5 risk feature explosion and overfitting (p.341).
Inspect largest coefficients to introspect text models (p.338-343).
Try lemmatization or stemming when squeezing out performance, especially for small datasets (p.347).
For topic models drop very common words (max_df) and verify topics by reading top documents (p.348, 355).
LDA topic weights can serve as a compact representation for supervised learning with few examples (p.355).

terms.definition: each data point, represented as a single text
discard structure of the input text and only count how often each word appears in each text in the corpus
split each document into tokens; collect and number all words in any document; count occurrences per document
give high weight to any term that appears often in a particular document, but not in many documents in the corpus
sequences of tokens; pairs are bigrams, triplets trigrams
rule-based heuristic, like dropping common suffixes, to conflate words with the same stem
a dictionary of known word forms is used and the role of the word in the sentence is taken into account; the standardized form is the lemma
umbrella term for assigning each document to one or multiple topics, usually without supervision
finds groups of words (topics) that appear together frequently; each document is a mixture of a subset of the topics
